title: Sub agents explained
source: Written from general knowledge of AI agents (sub agents, context window). No measured figures.

voice.style: Warm, clear explainer narrator. Unhurried and friendly, like showing a colleague a neat trick.
voice.outroStyle: Calm and warm, a short takeaway.

lines.text: Give one AI every single job, and sooner or later it drowns.
The fix: hand some of it to sub agents.
Every file it reads and every command it runs takes space in its working memory.
Near full, it gets slow, costly, and starts forgetting older details.
A sub agent is a helper AI with exactly one task.
It works in its own memory, reads dozens of files, and reports back only the answer.
Bigger job? Call several helpers at once.
One scans the code, one writes tests, one reviews.
An hour one by one becomes a few minutes in parallel.
Lots of reading, only a conclusion needed? Delegate it.
Needs every detail in mind? The main AI keeps it.
So the main AI stays clear-headed for the hardest part: making the call.
Sub agents: split the work, keep a clear head.
Save this for your next project.
